changes: Removed 'Vidyārathi' as a separate person: vidyārathi(!) = vidyārthī 'student', an epithet of the scribe Motirāma ('likhitaṃ motirāma vidyārthī'), now in his titles
Haranārāyaṇa: the son relation now points to Motirāma (putrasya = 'of [his] son'), and the owner role is kept at low confidence; an alternative reading is given in notes
Dropped the son_of relation to the non-person 'Vidyārathi'
Lowered the confidence of the Haranārāyaṇa identification

notes: 'śrīrāma' at the start is an invocation, not a name. 'vidyārathi(!)' is very likely a corruption of vidyārthī 'student', describing Motirāma, and not a father's name. 'putrasya haranārāyaṇa' has broken syntax. The reading used here is '[copy] of [his] son Haranārāyaṇa', i.e. written by the student Motirāma for his son Haranārāyaṇa. Another possible reading is 'Motirāma, son of Haranārāyaṇa', with a Hindi-style misplaced genitive. In that case Haranārāyaṇa would be Motirāma's father (relative_only), the relation would be p1 son_of p2, and the owner role would go. The catalogue gives the scribe as '??'. The colophon is undated.
